items.text: Lakes State caretaker governor Rin Tueny Mabor, speaking in Rumbek, warned of possible hunger, saying May and June rainfall was insufficient for cultivation and rains that began in October came too late for this year's farming season; he said northern parts of the state face serious water and pasture shortages and cattle keepers may move herds towards southern Lakes and neighbouring areas (county not stated).

WFP's Matthew Hollingworth says the agency faces an $86 million funding gap now and a further $416 million gap over the next six months, and warns that more than one million vulnerable people could lose access to lifesaving food and nutrition assistance by October unless additional funding is secured; he says 7.8 million people struggle to find food each day as South Sudan faces conflict, displacement, economic hardship and climate shocks. At Canal Pigi in Jonglei he met families whose farmland has stayed flooded seven years after the original floods, while drought affects the remaining land.

In a precautionary notice, the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation warns of possible Nile flooding in vulnerable areas in and around Juba: hydrological simulations suggest Lake Victoria could rise significantly, potentially above its historical maximum, and the notice cites ICPAC's outlook of a higher El Nino likelihood with above-normal rain over the Lake Victoria basin and parts of the wider Nile basin. Readings from Nimule to Renk and Nasir to Bentiu are decreasing and remain below flood-alert levels. Reduced June-September rainfall has also affected several states and the administrative areas of Abyei, Pibor and Ruweng.

Flooding has submerged about 70% of the land in Bentiu, and the dykes built and maintained around the clock by UNMISS and IOM protect about 300,000 people. UNMISS's Bentiu field office head says 50,000 people would be submerged if UN and IOM work were affected and a dyke breach were not repaired within ten hours, and that IOM faces a shortage of resources for dyke maintenance and pumping; he expects heavy rain with El Nino from October to February (county inferred from Bentiu).

State health officials, including the Ministry of Health's health education focal point Luka Lual Aliue, report 40 hepatitis E cases, no deaths so far, in epidemiological weeks 38 and 39 in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (counties including Aweil East, Aweil North, Gok Machar and Aweil West); health officials link the surge to water sources contaminated during the rainy season.
